claims.title: Which maps of abelian schemes give the transitions in the tower?
claims.hypotheses: The marked unitary moduli problem has its principal-level integral models and the prime-to-p torsion comparisons. The adelic element preserves the lattice and conjugates the finer level into the target level.
claims.statement: At a sufficiently fine principal level the quotient by the specified torsion subgroup constructs the required isogeny and its prime-to-p quasi-inverse scalar. A compatible pair for a fixed label is unique when it exists, and composite pairs realize the ordered product of their labels.

claims.hypotheses: The quotient isogeny has been constructed on a finer level, and the level and lattice inclusions are satisfied.

claims.title: Which level changes give finite étale covers?
claims.hypotheses: Two admissible principal level subgroups are nested. A free transitive quotient action is asserted for a normal inclusion.
claims.statement: The identity-labelled transition is a finite étale surjection on fibre powers. Under normality the quotient group acts freely and transitively on its geometric fibres. A common normal refinement permits counting for an arbitrary inclusion.

claims.title: How does a trace give a class with all the prescribed Hecke eigenvalues?
claims.hypotheses: The uniform weighted trace comparisons and the spectral word test hold for the prescribed scalars and nonnegative dominant weight on the complex tower.
claims.statement: For each prescribed exponent one coherent cohomology degree contains a nonzero common eigenvector for the entire operator family. One fibre power suffices for the levels and conjugates in the comparison.

claims.title: Which coefficient of the holomorphic trace detects a prescribed degree?
claims.hypotheses: The transverse fixed-point formula, weighted comparison of marked fixed points and definite pairs, algebraic weight calculation and definite automorphic trace comparison apply to the admitted test.
claims.statement: In the signed holomorphic trace polynomial the coefficient at each admissible exponent is the definite trace. Undoing the holomorphic sign gives a nonzero alternating coherent trace whenever the definite trace is nonzero.

claims.title: Which components of the integral model does the tower reach?
claims.hypotheses: A discrete valuation ring carries a smooth projective model. The map of the tower to the generic fibre is finite étale.
claims.statement: The generic image extends uniquely to an open and closed part of the integral model. The restricted generic cover is surjective and the relative dimension, smoothness and projectivity persist.

claims.title: Why does the restriction preserve good reduction?
claims.hypotheses: An initial local model has for each tower operator a finite étale source of constant degree and a compatible comparison to the pullback of positive multiplicity.
claims.statement: Restricting the model to the generic image gives a good-reduction witness with surjective generic cover. Both the source degree and the multiplicity of each comparison are preserved.
